hook.line: Buses, fog and traffic jams: running late is part of life in Bogotá. You will want to say whether you arrived on time, early or late, and whether the schedule slipped.

examples.en: I arrived late for the meeting.

examples.es: El vuelo salió con retraso por la niebla.
examples.en: The flight left late because of the fog.

rule:
With *llegar*: *a tiempo* is on time, *temprano* is early, *tarde* is late. English "in time" becomes *a tiempo*.

*Temprano* and *tarde* never change for a man or a woman.

When the schedule slips, say *con retraso* or *retrasado*: *el vuelo salió con retraso*. A person who is always on time is *puntual*.

Rushing is a different idea: for that, Colombians say *estoy de afán*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *temprano* and *tarde* adverbs of time, so they do not agree with the person.

options: I arrived early for the meeting.
I arrived on time for the meeting.
I arrived late for the meeting.

readAndPick.es: Salimos temprano para llegar a tiempo.
options: We left late to arrive on time.
We left on time to arrive early.
We left early to arrive on time.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Por suerte llegamos ___.* (*a tiempo* or *de tiempo*) Luckily we arrived on time.
Pick and type the whole sentence: *El vuelo salió ___ retraso.* (*con* or *en*) The flight left late.
Say: I arrived late for the meeting.
accept: Yo llegué tarde a la reunión.
yourTurn.why: *Llegué* is the *I* form and *tarde* means late.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Did you arrive early?
yourTurn.why: *Llegaste* is the informal *you* in the past, and *temprano* means early.
A bus runs on a schedule, so *retrasado* or *con retraso* fits.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it to early: *Llegué tarde a la reunión.*
yourTurn.why: Swap *tarde* for *temprano* and nothing else changes.
*No* goes in front of the verb.

pitfalls.why: English says "in time", but Spanish says *a tiempo*.
Almost. English says late *for*, but you arrive *a* somewhere: *tarde a la reunión*.
*Temprano* here is an adverb, so it stays the same for a woman.

personal: Say whether you usually arrive on time, early or late: *Siempre llego…* or *Casi nunca llego…*.
